title: Resolve a merge conflict
setup: git init -q . && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
printf 'Colors we like\nfavorite: red\n' > colors.txt && git add colors.txt && git commit -qm 'Add colors'
git checkout -q -b feature/blue && printf 'Colors we like\nfavorite: blue\n' > colors.txt && git add colors.txt && git commit -qm 'Prefer blue'
git checkout -q main && printf 'Colors we like\nfavorite: green\n' > colors.txt && git add colors.txt && git commit -qm 'Prefer green'

checks.name: no conflict markers are left in colors.txt
the favorite line reads: favorite: blue-green
nothing is left uncommitted (git status is clean)

hints: Start the merge with git merge feature/blue. It will stop and report the conflict.
Open colors.txt, delete the three marker lines, and leave one line: favorite: blue-green
Then git add colors.txt and git commit --no-edit.
